angle: treat the hands as two runners on one track: the minute hand runs 12 laps while the hour hand runs 1, so it laps it 12 - 1 = 11 times. Run the full 12 hours on screen and drop a dot at every meeting: 11 evenly spaced dots appear, and the gap between 11 and 1 shows which hour 'loses' its meeting. Then the off-by-a-bit times (3:16:22, not 3:15) and a checkable question (right angles: 22)
title: A clock's hands meet only 11 times in 12 hours
description:
The minute and hour hands of a clock line up only 11 times in 12 hours, not 12 (22 times a day). In 12 hours the minute hand runs 12 laps and the hour hand runs 1, and the faster hand catches the slower one once per lap it gains: 12 minus 1 is 11. Between 11 and 1 o'clock the hands meet only once, at exactly 12, and the meeting after 3 o'clock is at about 3:16:22, not 3:15. The meetings are evenly spaced, every 1 hour, 5 minutes and 27 seconds.

Checked with exact fractions (meetings at 12k/11 hours), a 1-second tick-by-tick run of the full 12 hours, and 200,000 random moments.
facts_checked: the hands meet at t = 12k/11 hours, k = 0..10: 11 times in 12 hours, 22 times a day
in 12 hours the minute hand turns 12 times, the hour hand once; 12 - 1 = 11 laps gained
1-second tick simulation over 12 hours counts 11 passes of the minute hand over the hour hand
the only meeting between 11:00 and 1:00 is 12:00 exactly
the meeting after 3 o'clock is at 3:16:21.8 (about 16 minutes and 22 seconds past three), not 3:15
meetings are 12/11 h = 1 h 5 min 27.3 s apart; 11 equal gaps fill 12 hours
simulation: 200,000 random moments, mean wait to the next meeting 0.5467 h vs exact 6/11 = 0.5455 h
closing answer: the hands are at right angles 22 times in 12 hours, not the naive 24 (and opposite 11 times)

beats.say: The hands of a clock meet only 11 times in 12 hours. Not 12.
That sounds wrong. The minute hand passes the hour hand once every hour. So, 12.
Think of it as a race on a round track. In 12 hours, the minute hand runs 12 laps. The hour hand runs just one.
Every time the fast runner laps the slow one, the hands meet. Watch them all.
12 laps, minus the 1 lap the hour hand ran. That leaves 11. And 22 a day.
So which hour loses its meeting? Between 11 and 1, they meet only once, at exactly 12.
And the meetings drift. After 3 o'clock, it's not a quarter past. It's about 16 minutes and 22 seconds past.
